1134.author: yuanzhou75
1134.body:
Closes #1125


## The defect

A delivered file's revision was registered with `new Date()` sampled *after* the copy, while the file on disk kept its own mtime — and when the bytes already existed, `copyCasToWorkspace({ reuseIdentical: true })` returned before touching the file at all. So the very next workspace listing compared `revision.modifiedAt` against `stat`, found them unequal, appended a revision built by `reconcileWorkspaceFiles`, and moved `currentRevisionId` onto it. That revision carries `origin: "unknown"`, no `contentHash`, no `publicationSequence`, no `artifactVersionIds`, and no `parentRevisionId` — so the provenance view lost the attribution *and* the lineage and the Artifact link, for a file whose bytes never changed.

The observed arrow is arithmetic, not a coincidence: the attributed row's `modifiedAt` is 25 ms *later* than the file's real mtime, which is exactly the clock read.

## The fix

All four clock-stamped registrations now record the file's own `stat.mtime`, matching the paths that already survive a listing (`services/api/src/papers.ts:339`, `packages/provenance/src/recorder.ts:386`):

| site | what it delivers |
| --- | --- |
| `services/api/src/artifacts/materialize.ts` | Artifact promotion |
| `services/api/src/remote-runner.ts` | a pull landing in the local root |
| `services/api/src/agent-run/workspace-bindings.ts` | a committed workspace transfer |
| `services/api/src/subagents/index.ts` | the handoff's first observation of files it has not seen yet |

`services/api/src/subagents/index.ts:121` is untouched — that is a listing object, not a revision registration. In the handoff case a file that no longer exists in the live workspace is skipped rather than stamped with a time that is known to be wrong.

**The reconcile branch is deliberately unchanged.** `reconcileWorkspaceFiles` receives only `path`/`modifiedAt`/`size` and no digest, so it cannot tell a clock read a few milliseconds late from a real same-size edit. Inheriting `origin`/`contentHash`/`artifactVersionIds` there would credit that edit to the previous producer and break `services/api/src/store.test.ts:679` (*marks an unrecorded Workspace overwrite as unknown*, which requires `origin === "unknown"` and `revisions.length === 3`). An unrecorded external edit keeps degrading to `unknown`, and there is a case for that below so the trade cannot be lost silently.

## Verification

`services/api/src/artifacts/materialize.test.ts`, two new cases:

1. **`a promoted version keeps its attribution across the listing that follows`** — `materializeArtifact` → `listWorkspaceFiles` twice → `getWorkspaceFileProvenance`: `origin === "system"`, `contentHash === version.content.hash`, `artifactVersionIds === [version.id]`, **and** `lineage` and `artifacts` unchanged with no revision appended; then a second `materializeArtifact` of the identical bytes (the early-return branch) followed by another listing, still attributed.
2. **`a same-size edit on disk still degrades to unknown`** — the behaviour the fix must not trade away.

Both were run here through a scratch copy with the tag relaxed to `os:windows`, and I checked they actually pin the defect rather than passing vacuously: with the `materialize.ts` stamp reverted to `new Date()`, case 1 fails on `listing pass 1 must not replace the delivered revision`; with the fix it passes. The committed tags stay `os:linux`, so CI is what runs them as written.

`tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json` and `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` report nothing for these files. The suites that exercise `remote-runner` and the transfer commit end to end are `os:linux`-tagged and are skipped on this Windows host — CI runs those, and I am not claiming a local run of them.

1139.author: yuanzhou75
1139.body:
Closes #1132

## The defect

The Evolve LLM proxy wrote one usage row per proxied completion — correct — but keyed it by the **run**: `invocationId: evolve:<runId>` with `attemptIndex` held at `0`. The ledger's idempotency key is `(sessionId, invocationId, invocationKind, attemptIndex)`, so the first row was written and calls 2..N were absorbed as replays of call 1. The absorbing `return` is not an error, so the only warning on that path (`evolve_llm_usage_unrecorded`, gated on an exception) could not fire. Nothing anywhere said the spend had been dropped.

Measured on a real environment: a 73-call research recorded **0.83%** of its tokens, an 85-call one **0.93%**, and the surviving row's `totalTokens`/`startedAt`/`finishedAt` bracket only the first call — the row kept is call 1, relabelled as the run. `usageStatus: "reported"` on it asserts the provider figures were captured, which is what makes the error silent rather than merely coarse.

## The fix

**One identity per call** (`llm-proxy.ts`): `invocationId: evolve:<runId>:<randomUUID>`, keeping `invocationKind: "evolve"` and the row's `runId`. This is the shape `evolution/direction-draft.ts:58-60` already uses for the same `invocationKind`, and it is the option the issue ranks first: the alternative (a monotone `attemptIndex` per run) needs a durable counter. Cost still aggregates per run, because aggregation reads `runId`, not the key.

**The drop stops being silent** (`store.ts`): the suppressing branch now names the key it absorbed. The deduplication itself is untouched — `store.test.ts:1184` pins that an intentional replay of the same attempt must still be absorbed, and that is the behaviour the ledger depends on. What changed is that a writer keying distinct calls the same way can no longer look like correct idempotency.

## What the regression case pins

`services/api/src/evolution/llm-proxy.test.ts` — *every proxied completion of one run keeps its own ledger identity*: three proxied completions for one run must produce three **distinct ledger keys** with one shared `runId`, `sessionId` and `invocationKind`, and `attemptIndex` staying `0` (these are distinct calls, not retries, and inventing an attempt index would say otherwise). The assertion counts distinct keys rather than distinct `invocationId`s, because the key is what the real ledger deduplicates on.

I deliberately did **not** write §7.4 as literally worded ("N appends with the same run-scoped `invocationId` … must not collapse to one row"): that would require the ledger to distinguish rows by `id`, contradicting `store.test.ts:1184` and the contract in `model-usage.test.ts:83`. The call axis belongs to the writer, and that is where both the defect and the test sit.

Checked that the case fails for the right reason: with the run-scoped `invocationId` restored it fails on `each call carries its own ledger identity, so no call is read as a replay`.

## Verification

- `tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json` and `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json`: nothing for these files.
- `evolution/llm-proxy.test.ts` **18/18** and the `store.test.ts` dedup case pass here through a tag-relaxed copy — the latter while emitting the new `model_usage_append_deduplicated: task logical-call attempt 0 in session …` line, which is the observability part working.
- Both suites are tagged `os:linux`, so the committed files are what CI runs, not my relaxed copy.

## Not claimed

No backfill: calls 2..N are not recoverable from the ledger, as the issue states. I also did not change the `usageStatus` vocabulary, so a row still reports what the provider sent for that call.

1139.title: fix(api): give every proxied Evolve completion its own ledger identity

1141.author: yuanzhou75
1141.body:
Relates #1133. This PR changes the recorder contract and the trajectory snapshot; the measured tool-only row class in #1133 is not restored here, so the issue stays open until its `need-human` question is answered.

## The defect

`AgentVersionRecorder` kept the link between a model call and the provider response it belongs to in **one mutable field** (`versioning.ts:156`). It was written synchronously by the event path (`response_start` → `:247`) and read *later, when the recording queue drained*, by `modelCompleted` (`:259`). `beforeTurn` (`:189`) and `afterAssembly` (`:215`) clear that field from inside the same queue, so a completion could be written after the next turn had already cleared it.

The report measured the consequence: **54 of 303** `model.completed` records carried no `responseId` although a `response_start` at the same turn had issued one; in the deterministic shape the recorder returned `turn: 2` and no id for a response `r1` that belonged to turn 1.

## The fix

- **The identity is data, not process state.** `modelCompleted(result, identity?)` takes `{ turn, responseId }`. A caller that sees `assistant.response.started` passes it; a supplied identity wins over the recorder's field, and `responseId: undefined` means *"this call has none"*, so a stale value is **dropped** instead of attributing the record to a neighbouring response (§7 of the report warned about exactly that mis-binding).
- **Without an explicit identity the evidence is snapshotted when the call completes**, not when the queue drains — the field is still valid at that moment in the built-in loop, whose `response_start` precedes the completion.
- **`JiuwenSwarmTrajectory` remembers the id it announced for the call** (`jiuwenswarm-trajectory.ts`) and passes it into the completion record; it is cleared when a new `modelRequest` starts, so the value handed to the record belongs to the call that just answered rather than to whatever the recorder happens to hold.

The recorder's field is still maintained for the evidence that other events carry (`assistant.response.started` itself, `state.committed`), so nothing else about the evidence shape changes.

## Verification

`services/api/src/native-agent/versioning.test.ts`, two new cases:

1. **`a completion record keeps the response id of the call it answers`** — `response_start r1 turn 1`, then a completion whose write is still queued while the next turn's `beforeTurn` clears the field. Asserts `responseId === "r1"` and `turn === 1`.
2. **`an identity passed by the caller wins over a recorder field that has moved on`** — the field has already advanced to turn 2; the caller passes `{ turn: 1, responseId: "r9" }` and the record carries exactly that.

**Mutation check:** reverting `modelCompleted` to read the evidence after `await this.pending` (the pre-fix ordering) turns **both** cases red with `actual: undefined`; with the fix they pass. `versioning.test.ts` 6/6, `jiuwenswarm-agent.test.ts`'s trajectory case still passes.

`tsc -p services/api --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` are clean. The two suites carry `os:linux`; their tags were relaxed for this Windows host and restored before pushing, so CI runs them as written. I did **not** re-run a live JiuwenSwarm session, so the 54/303 rate is not re-measured here — the fix is pinned by the deterministic cases above.

## Not changed on purpose

- The turn a completion records still comes from the recorder's counter when no identity is passed; the report classifies per-call turn drift as *structurally possible but not observable in the data*, and changing the turn contract needs the gateway to hand the call's turn back to the trajectory — a separate change.
- `reconcile`-style fallbacks in the trajectory server and the web timeline are untouched: they now simply receive an id where they previously guessed.

1143.author: yuanzhou75
1143.body:
Closes #1135.

## The defect

`scripts/start-stack.test.mjs::a leftover backup from a hard kill is restored on the next start` polled for the fixture file's **existence** and then read its **content**:

```js
`#!/bin/sh\ncat uv.lock > "${seenFile}"\nexit 0\n`   // :139
await waitFor(() => existsSync(seenFile), ...)         // :144
assert.equal(await readFile(seenFile, "utf8"), PRISTINE, ...)  // :145
```

The shell performs the `>` redirection — creating and truncating the target — **before** `cat` runs, so `existsSync` can return while the file is still zero bytes and the assertion reads `''`. That is the failure quoted in #1135 (`+ ''` vs `- 'version = 1\n# committed resolution\n'`), observed twice on the same head 13 minutes apart; a re-run did not clear it.

## The fix (test-only, both directions the issue suggested)

- **The polled path only ever appears complete.** The fake uv writes to `<seenFile>.tmp` and `mv`s it into place, so existence now implies completeness.
- **The wait is on the content the assertion wants**, so poll and assertion agree on what "the sync ran" means:
  `waitFor(async () => (await readFile(seenFile, "utf8").catch(() => "")) === PRISTINE, ...)`.
- **The same shape in the SIGTERM case is fixed too.** `echo $$ > uv.pid` has the identical truncate-before-write window; that case was safe only because the *next* wait reads `uv.lock` first. It now waits for a parseable pid. No assertion was relaxed, nothing was given a sleep, `PRISTINE` is untouched, and no case was skipped or re-tagged.

## Verification

The file carries `os:linux` and its fake `uv` is a POSIX shell script that the launcher spawns directly, so **it cannot execute on this Windows host** — the unmodified `main` version times out the same way (`timed out waiting for the fake uv to start` / `timed out waiting for the first sync to run`, ~30 s each), which is a host limitation, not this change.

What I could measure here is the mechanism itself, with a harness that recreates the fixture exactly (same `sh`, same redirection, same poll-then-read, 300 iterations each):

| synchronisation | incomplete reads |
| --- | --- |
| pre-fix: `existsSync` then read | **180 / 300** |
| fixed: tmp + `mv`, poll the content | **0 / 300** |

`sh -n` on the new fake-uv snippet is clean, so the shell change is valid POSIX. `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` reports nothing.

CI is what runs the real file as written: `UT` exercises the fixture itself, so the case that used to fail on an empty read now runs on every push instead of only on a loaded runner.

Relates #1133 (the issue stays open under `need-human` for the policy question it records).

## Why this is a follow-up

#1141 landed the per-call binding: a caller that sees `assistant.response.started` passes the id, and a completion whose write is still queued no longer loses an id that had already been issued. HongyeZhou then pointed out the class it does not cover: **a call with no text and no reasoning gets its response opened by the adapter after the completion has been requested** (`services/adapter/src/sciencediscovery_adapter/events.py:152-162`), so no caller can pass that id — and the first cut deleted the recorder's value whenever an identity was supplied, leaving exactly the tool-only rows anonymous.

## What changed

- `completedEvidence` takes the caller's id when it has one, and otherwise falls back to the recorder's value **only when that value was announced for the same turn**. The recorder now remembers which turn its `responseId` belongs to (`responseIdTurn`), set with the id and cleared at both existing clearing points.
- The completion write therefore picks up an id minted after it was requested, while a leftover from a neighbouring turn is still never attributed to this record — "dropped" cannot silently become "mis-bound".
- `modelCompleted` keeps the call-time snapshot for callers that supply no identity at all (the built-in loop, whose `response_start` already arrived), and re-reads at write time only for the late-mint case.

## Verification

`services/api/src/native-agent/versioning.test.ts` 8/8 with the tag relaxed for this Windows host and restored before pushing:

- a response id minted **after** the completion was requested still reaches the record (`late-1`);
- an id belonging to **another turn** is never reused for this record;
- the two cases #1141 added still pass (queued write surviving the next turn's clearing; a supplied identity winning over a moved-on field).

Mutation checks, both red before the fix and green after: removing the fallback turns the late-id case red (`actual: undefined`); reading the evidence after the queue drain turns the first case red. `tsc -p services/api` and `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` are clean.

## Residual (stated, not closed)

The fallback restores parity with main before #1141: it reads at the point the completion write drains, now guarded by the turn the id was announced for. It does **not** move that read past the moment the tool-only rows lost the id — the adapter mints those ids in another process and channel, and nothing orders that mint against the recorder's drain. So the class is restored **only when the mint beats the drain**; the rest stays for the backfill/bounded-wait/§7.2 choice #1133 keeps under 
eed-human.

The late-id test pins the favourable ordering (an id announced between the call and the write), not a real adapter mint landing inside that window; that is what the test can assert without a live swarm instance.

Known cosmetic: this comment line carries one stray CR where the backtick before "responseId" belongs (ersioning.ts:157) — comment text only, fixed in the next change to this file rather than in another review cycle here.

1148.body:
Relates #1140 — items 7.1, 7.2, 7.4 and 7.5 land here; 7.3 is dropped and argued on the issue

## What the user sees today, and what changes

A long-trajectory session's dialog showed three false things at once: a raw browser string (`signal is aborted without reason`), a claim that the session had no workspace files while it had 176, and two disabled export buttons. None of that was a server error — the preview was merely slow, and the caller had left.

**1. The dialog recognises its own cancellation.** `export-preview-cache.ts` aborted with no reason, so Chromium manufactured that string and `errorText` rendered it verbatim. It now aborts with `PreviewBudgetExpired` (name `AbortError`, so the existing `isAbortError` in `apps/web/src/api/client.ts` matches), and the dialog turns that — and the server's existing `EXPORT_PREVIEW_PENDING` answer — into a localized "still preparing, it retries automatically" status line instead of an error.

**2. "Not determined" is no longer rendered as "empty".** The empty state was `!files.length ? noWorkspaceFiles : null`, true for a preview that had not arrived. It now speaks only for a successful preview. Two new keys, both locales.

**3. A slow preview is served by later polls, not by a timer.** The route still holds the request open for as long as the work takes; what is truthful now is the client side of it — the dialog names its own 10 s cancellation and shows the retrying state instead of a browser string, and its 3 s poll picks the result up when the server finishes. No wall-clock budget is imposed on `defaults()`: an earlier revision of this branch added one and it answered 202 to a fixture that legitimately needs ~49 s, because a clock cannot tell "slow but finishing" from "pathological". A pending-for-slow rule has to key off queue starvation rather than elapsed time, and that is not in this PR (see the issue's §7.3).

**4. One session's dialog no longer waits behind another's.** The service had a single serial chain for every project and session; it is now one chain per `projectId:sessionId`. Ordering *within* a session — and the deadlock hazard the code warns about — is unchanged, and `close()` drains every chain.

**5. §7.4: one closure walk per revision, not one per profile.** Two of the five profiles carry the full trajectory and each hydrated the same 3.2 GB / 7 740-object closure independently. The sizing pass records what the walk produced, keyed by **walk shape and session** (`full:` / `summary:`) and by evidence revision: one byte count, the CAS hashes and the version refs per entry, in order. The second full-trajectory profile replays those numbers instead of re-reading the records, and a summarized walk can never feed a full one. The replay reproduces `estimatedBytes` exactly, including the comma accounting, which depends on entry order. Only measurements are cached, never a detail object: #1085 was lost to keeping entries alive.

## What this does not do

- **§7.3 (make "slow" answer like "busy")** is deliberately dropped — see above and the comment on the issue.
- **§7.6 (sizing without deserialising)** is **not done**, and I had its premise wrong in an earlier revision of this description: I wrote that the preview path contains no `readRecord`, on the strength of `research-snapshots.ts` alone. It does — `packages/trajectory/src/server.ts:69` (`await store.readRecord(ref, kind)`) and `:312` (`await store.readRecord(event.payloadRef)`) resolve every trajectory detail the walk asks for, so each entry the preview sizes is a record read plus a JSON parse. That is what §7.4 above removes half of, and it is why the issue's cost model holds. What remains for §7.6 proper is reading only the dependency list instead of deserialising whole records, which is a change of its own.
- **§7.7 / §7.8** are untouched.

## Rendered evidence for the two new states

Both locales, before and after, of the export dialog. These are renderer-level
captures: the component's markup with the app's own `tokens.css` / `base.css` /
`primitives.css` / `dialogs.css` and the real `messages.ts` strings, rendered in
Chromium. They are not Electron-window captures and not a live interaction.

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| en | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1148/docs/screenshots/1148/1148-en-before-v2.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1148/docs/screenshots/1148/1148-en-after-v2.png) |
| zh | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1148/docs/screenshots/1148/1148-zh-before-v2.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1148/docs/screenshots/1148/1148-zh-after-v2.png) |

These four were re-rendered on request. The first version's Chinese captures were
garbled — the capture script decoded every message string with
`.encode().decode("unicode_escape")`, which turns UTF-8 Chinese into latin-1
(`仍在准备` → `ä»å¨å¤‡`); ASCII was unaffected, so only the Chinese ones were garbage. The
fix decodes with `json.loads` and names CJK fallbacks explicitly, and the
custom-content section is expanded so the two states are actually visible. Checked
without looking at the images: the corrected pages carry the exact `messages.ts`
strings with zero latin-1 mojibake runs, and segmenting the ink in the PNG gives
18 glyph segments with 16 distinct shapes for the scope line — fallback boxes would
be one shape repeated.

**before** is today's behaviour: the status line carries Chromium's own
`signal is aborted without reason`, and the custom-content section claims the
session has no workspace files. **after** is this branch: a localized "still
preparing, it retries automatically" status line, and "the export scope has not
been determined yet" instead of an empty claim.

That the stylesheet is actually applied was checked rather than assumed, since a
capture with no styles looks plausible until someone reads it: a headless probe
over the same document reports `.research-export-dialog` at `width: 620px`
(matching `dialogs.css`), `display: flex`, background `rgb(255,255,255)`, heading
ink `rgb(52, 64, 84)` and the selected card's border `rgb(154, 184, 236)` — i.e.
the theme tokens resolved.

**One limit I am stating plainly:** I cannot view images, so this is a
programmatic check of layout and tokens plus the exact strings from `messages.ts`,
not an eye check. The wording decisions are the reviewers' and the user's to
accept; the author approval is still pending and this PR should not be read as
claiming otherwise.

## Verification

- `tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json` and `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json`: clean for every file this PR touches. (The three `evolution/proposal.ts` errors are this checkout's stale schema and are present without these changes; to make the check meaningful I also synced `memory-watch.ts`, `heap-budget.ts` and `trajectory.ts` from `main`, which this tree was missing.)
- `tsc` over `apps/web` scoped to the two changed files: clean.
- CI on head `1ac9ee256bb6`: `UT`, `merge-gate`, `L1`, `ST`, `Coverage`, `Docker image`, both `Binary release`s and `CodeCheck` all pass, no red, nothing skipped that matters.
- The existing serialization assertions still hold by construction: the chain is per session, so one dialog's five profiles still run one at a time (`peak === 1`), and a second `get()` for the same session joins the same chain.
- **New regression case** (`services/api/src/research-preview-trajectory-replay.test.ts`, new file, no existing fixture touched): seeding `full:<sessionId>` with a number no empty session's real walk can produce shows the replay branch reads the map; an empty cache adds nothing and must still gain the `full:<sessionId>` key, which pins the **write** — the defect both reviewers caught; a `summary:<sessionId>` entry is ignored by a full walk, pinning the shape key. The same file also covers the replay branch's own omission push and the receipt's bound: a seeded `full:<sessionId>` entry that names an unreadable record has to reappear in `omissions` when a later profile replays that walk (deleting the replay push at `research-snapshots.ts:441` turns the case red), and a seeded list two past `TRAJECTORY_OMISSION_LIMIT` makes the receipt name exactly five entries and report the two it withheld (disabling the overflow line at `:485` turns that case red). Boundary, stated narrowly: this proves the replay reads and the walk writes that map; it does **not** observe `readTrajectoryDetail` not being called, because that closure is not exported.
- **Unreadable-record omission** (`research-preview-trajectory-replay.test.ts`): one `agent.record` stream event whose `payloadRef` names an object that was never written makes the lazy loader throw for that entry only, and the case asserts the **session-scoped prefix** `trajectory:<sessionId>:` reaches the returned `omissions` — it does not pin the entry id. The two seeded cases above do pin exact strings, because those strings are the test's own. It drives the export path (the first walk, `:458`); the replaying profile's own push at `:441` is the seeded case above, which is the part the export case cannot reach.
- **Rendered evidence** for the two new states is in the section above: both locales, before and after, with the programmatic check that the stylesheet and theme tokens actually applied.

## What this changes

Imported Evolve runs and events remain readable when the Evolve service is not initialized, so a session restored from a research package can show its task card and process. New Evolve operations stay gated by service readiness.

- `services/api/src/http/index.ts` exempts the three read-only routes — `GET /api/evolve/runs`, its `events`, and a candidate's source — from the readiness gate. Authentication still runs first, and `stop`, the idea-tree routes and every other `/api/evolve/*` path keep the gate.

- `apps/desktop/src/evolve/use-evolve.ts` does the same: with a session open, the run list is read whether or not the runtime is initialized. Readiness now gates starting a search, not reading what already happened — without this the desktop client, the one that ships, still hid the restored card.

## Tests

- **Web** (`apps/web/tests/EvolveRunPolling.test.tsx`): the case that encoded the old contract is rewritten rather than dropped — a session id reads and delivers its restored runs while `ready` is false, an absent session id reads nothing and clears the list, a readiness change re-reads and discards the superseded answer, and unmount drops a late result. 1153.author: yuanzhou75
1153.body:
Relates #1133 — the deterministic-id half of it. The issue's second `need-human` item is "where the response id is minted", and this takes option (a): at the model-call boundary. It stays `Relates` because closing the issue should also show one measured run where no completion is anonymous, and this host cannot produce that run (the adapter runtime is not installed here), so the issue is left to close on that evidence rather than on this claim.

## Why the previous two attempts could not close it

#1141 bound the id per call and #1145 made a *late* id reusable by its own turn, but both still needed the adapter to announce first. For a turn that answers with only a tool call there is nothing to announce until Swarm has received the tool call, which is after this side has already written the record:

- the gateway streams the `tool_calls` frame (`services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts:556`) and then writes `model.completed` (`:558`);
- the adapter opens the response only when Swarm replays it as `chat.tool_call` (`services/adapter/src/sciencediscovery_adapter/events.py:152-162`, `:232-264`), minting a fresh `uuid4` there.

Two processes, two streams, no ordering. That is why #1145 had to state its residual as "restored only when the mint beats the drain".

## What changed

- **The call is an object, not a value.** The gateway mints `call = { responseId }` for every task call before the request leaves, passes it into `request(...)` so the queued `model_request` binds that call to the turn it opens, and passes it back into `completed(...)`. `modelCompleted` reads its own identity and its own turn; nothing shared is read across calls, so dispatch A → dispatch B → complete A cannot stamp A with B's id or B's turn. Housekeeping is not recorded, so it never gets an identity.
- **The id travels back with the response** in `x-sciencediscovery-response-id`, on the streaming and the JSON response.
- **The adapter's proxy keeps it** (`llm_proxy.py`): the header is stripped before the response is forwarded on to Swarm — Swarm has no use for it — and queued on the run's route, oldest first.
- **The mapper claims it** (`events.py::_open_response`) when it announces that response. A Swarm pointed at something other than this run's gateway dispatches no id and keeps the locally minted uuid, unchanged.
- **A stale adapter is *best-effort* visible.** The recorder remembers the id each turn's `model.completed` was written with, and compares an announcement against it — but only when that announcement is the last record still outstanding for the run, because with another call in flight the announcement may belong to that one and a false alarm sends an operator after a swap that did not happen. Two cases are therefore **not** compared: an announcement that arrives after the next call has already opened, and any mismatch that arrives while a stale entry is still waiting. The id on the record itself never depends on this comparison.

## Verification

- `tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit`: clean.
- `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.test.ts`: **63 / 64**. The one failure asserts `stat().mode & 0o777 === 0o600`, a Unix permission Windows cannot express; it fails the same way with this change reverted.
- `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.test.ts`: **117 / 118**. The one failure expects `/data/skill-snapshots/...` but Windows yields `\data\skill-snapshots\...`; both files were run with the `os` tag relaxed to this host and restored before pushing.
- New cases:
  - the id is settled **before** the streamer runs, equals the header the adapter receives, and is the identity the completion is recorded under;
  - a housekeeping call carries no header and is never named;
  - **interleaving**: dispatch A, dispatch B, then complete A and B → `[[turn 0, id-a], [turn 1, id-b]]`, each call keeping its own id and turn;
  - **stale adapter**: a call recorded as `recorded-id`, then an announcement of `adapter-own` → the warning names both;
  - the fake adapter echoes the header value as the id it announces, so the record id and the event id are asserted to be the same value end to end.
- **The adapter pytest suite was not run by me here**: `fastapi` is not installed on this host, so `test_events.py` and `test_llm_proxy.py` (two new cases each) are the CI's to run. The review bot ran them on a clean tree at this content (`test_llm_proxy.py`, `test_events.py`, `test_agent_runs.py`: 163 passed).

## Deployment note

API and adapter agree on the id through one header and ship from one repository. With an older adapter the record is still named while the announced event carries the adapter's own uuid; that mismatch is logged when the announcement is the only outstanding one, and stays quiet otherwise.

## Not changed

- The built-in runtime keeps its own path: `completedEvidence`'s turn guard and its fallback to the recorder's field are untouched, and remain the fallback when a call arrives without an identity.
- `callTurns` entries for a call that never completes are not pruned. Pruning by turn would drop the entry of a call still in flight and reintroduce the swap; a failure hook on the observer is the right shape and is not added here.
- The stale-adapter diagnostic is not keyed on the turn the adapter announced. That is the right shape and is filed as a follow-up rather than patched inside this branch: it needs proof that the adapter's turn counter and the trajectory's agree on every path, and a wrong key would turn a silent miss into a wrong warning.
- No live JiuwenSwarm run was re-measured, so the 54/303 rate is not re-derived; the fix is pinned by the ordering, interleaving and stale-adapter tests above.

1170.body:
Relates #1140 — §7.8 of the issue, split off from #1148 so the cost item gets its own review.

## The defect

A dialog open computes **five** preview profiles in one request (`defaults()`), and each profile listed the session's workspace twice: once inside `buildResearchPackageInput` (`services/api/src/research-snapshots.ts:494`) and once more to build the file rows for the response (`:765`). Measured on the new test, that is **ten scans and ten `reconcileWorkspaceFiles` calls** for one read-only size estimate — the "five directory *writes* to produce one read-only estimate" the issue names, with the intra-profile duplicate doubling it.

## What changed

- `PreviewSizing` carries `workspaceListings`, and `previewWorkspaceListing` reuses the complete listing for a **1 s window** per session, mirroring the bounded UI listing that already works this way (`services/api/src/artifacts/index.ts:85`).
- The cache is dropped as soon as the evidence revision moves (`workspaceListingsFor`), like the trajectory sizing cache next to it.
- Both call sites go through it, so a profile no longer scans its session a second time to answer with its file rows.

**Why a time window and not "once per request".** The calculator callback that `defaults()` fans out to is constructed per profile, with no request identity threaded to it, and the export path shares the same function. A revision-scoped cache without a bound would let a listing hide a file written after the first profile; a 1 s window covers the burst a dialog makes (all five run back to back) while a later request re-scans. Stated plainly: this is a bounded window, not a request-scoped guarantee, and the test does not measure the window — only that a burst shares one scan.

## Verification

- `tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit`: clean.
- New case `services/api/src/research-preview-workspace-listing.test.ts` (new file, `os:linux`, so CI executes it): spies `SessionStore.prototype.reconcileWorkspaceFiles` with a call-through wrapper, calls `exportPreviews.defaults(projectId, sessionId)`, asserts **one** reconcile for the request.
- **Mutation check:** forcing `previewWorkspaceListing` to never reuse turns the case red with `actual: [id × 10]`, `expected: [id]` — the pre-change cost, measured rather than asserted from the description.
- `services/api/src/research-preview-trajectory-replay.test.ts`: 6/6 still pass with the shared listing in place (that file drives `buildResearchPackageInput` directly with its own preview object, which has no `workspaceListings` and takes the unchanged path).

## Not changed

- §7.6 (sizing without deserialising), §7.3 (pending-for-slow) and §7.7 stay open on #1140; this PR does not claim them.
- The complete listing itself is unchanged for real exports: `listWorkspaceFiles(store, sessionId, true)` still scans fully and still never reuses a bounded UI listing — only a listing obtained the same way and within the same second is shared.

1171.author: yuanzhou75
1171.body:
Closes #1154.

## What this adds

A finished study-package export is now remembered by the desktop shell, so the package can be found again after the export dialog closes or the app restarts — and 打开文件位置 still works for packages saved in an earlier run.

**Shell** (`win_desktop`)

- `export-history.ts` — a small, self-managed `export-history.json` under `userData` (same temp-file-then-rename discipline as `export-state.ts` / `window-state.ts`). One row per export task: `id`, `token`, `path`, `filename`, `bytes`, `savedAt`, `projectId`, `sessionId`, `sessionTitle`, `level`. Newest first, bounded at 200 rows; eviction drops the record, never the user's file. A missing or corrupt file reads as an empty list instead of failing the start.
- `main.ts` — `export-write` records the row **after** the write succeeds, so a canceled or failed export leaves nothing behind; the write carries the export's own metadata (`recordId`, session, profile), and a re-save of the same task updates that task's row rather than adding a second one. Three IPC handlers: `export-history-list` (rows plus a `stat`-based `exists`, read with `fs.promises.stat` so a package on a slow share cannot block the main process), `export-history-reveal` (resolves the token from the persisted row, so it works after a restart; reports `missing` for a moved/deleted file instead of a silent no-op), `export-history-forget`.
- `preload.ts` — exposes `exportHistory` on `sdShell`, additive next to `exportFile`.

**Desktop UI** (`apps/desktop`)

- The session header now carries 导出 (`SessionBar` → the same export surface the session row menu opens).
- The export dialog's 已保存的会话包 block reads the durable list for the session the dialog is packaging — the id travels on the export record itself, because packaging outlives the dialog and the live request is not the exporting session by the time the write lands. Closing and reopening the dialog no longer empties it; failed packaging/saving rows keep their retry affordance.
- 设置 › 工作区 › 导出记录 lists every saved package across sessions and projects, with a filename/session search and a project filter, plus 打开文件位置 and 移除记录 per row. A row whose file was moved or deleted stays listed with 文件已被移动或删除 and can be removed — never silently dropped. A filter that matches nothing says so instead of claiming the feature is desktop-only.
- zh-CN and en copy; all strings live in `text/{zh,en}.ts`. A long session title ellipsizes instead of widening the row past the pane.

## The three decisions the review asked a person for

1. **Delivered independently of #1024's phase 2.** This is the narrow slice #1154 describes (a durable list plus where it is reachable); it does not build a new export panel, so #1024 can still redesign the surface without a second history implementation to retire.
2. **Full slice delivered in one PR, no follow-up issue.** The header entry, the settings group with search/filter, the missing-file state and the removal are all here — the acceptance criteria are met as written, so nothing is deferred.
3. **The browser (`apps/web`) shows no history.** A browser has no shell token to reveal and nothing the product wrote that it could point at; a localStorage copy would be a second history with different semantics (and no reveal), which the issue does not authorise. The settings pane says this instead. The desktop shell is the shipping client and the one this issue is about.

On dedupe: the row's key is the export task id, not the token — a re-save issues a new token, so token-keyed dedupe would turn "save to a new folder" into a second row (the contradiction the review flagged). The token is stored *on* the row and updated when the task is re-saved.

## Review findings, addressed

- A write that finishes after another session's dialog opened is filed under the **exporting** session: `ExportRecord` now carries `sessionId`, captured where the record is created, and the write meta sends it.
- The dialog's saved block is scoped to one session; with no session id it shows nothing rather than every session's packages.
- A long session title gets its own shrinkable, ellipsized span (`min-width: 0; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis`), and the row no longer widens the pane.
- `export-history-list` stats files with `fs.promises.stat`, not `statSync`, so a slow network share cannot block the Electron main process.
- A settings filter that matches nothing has its own copy (`noMatch`), distinct from "only available in the desktop app".
- `ExportDestinations.forget` is covered in `win_desktop/test/export-tokens.test.ts`, and the settings pane has its own component test (rows render, no-match copy, desktop-only fallback).

## Verification

- `win_desktop`: `node --test test/*.test.ts` → **238 passed, 0 failed**, including the history store (missing/corrupt file, restart round-trip, re-save updates the row and its token, bound eviction, forget, invalid rows dropped) and the token-forget case. Mutation: removing the upsert in `record()` fails 4 of its 7 cases.
- `apps/desktop`: new `export-history-list.test.tsx` 4/4 (row content, missing state hides reveal, both actions reach their callbacks with the right row, size/time formatting), new `export-history-settings.test.tsx` 2/2 (rows render; a filter matching nothing shows the no-match copy, not the desktop-only one), and the existing `settings-pages.test.tsx` 46/46 after the group list gained 导出记录 — all with `os:linux` relaxed locally for the run, tags restored before pushing. Mutation: showing 打开文件位置 for a missing row fails the first file; reverting the no-match copy fails the second.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean for `apps/desktop`, `apps/web`, `services/api`, `win_desktop` and the root `tsconfig.tests.json`; desktop `vite build` succeeds.
- `pnpm ci:l1` was not run on this host (it needs the full CI harness); CI runs it.

## Screenshots

Desktop renderer, mocked shell + control plane, 1440×900.

**The dialog's 已保存的会话包 block, before and after.** "Before" is the same tree with the previous bridge (no durable history), which is exactly the old behaviour: a package saved in an earlier run leaves the block empty.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |

1173.author: yuanzhou75
1173.body:
Refs #1152 — this is **stage 1** of the issue's own two-stage plan. The cap becomes one visible, enforced value; the streaming pass that lets the default move to 5 GiB is stage 2 and stays tracked in #1152.

## What changes

**One cap, one place.** `packages/research-package/src/index.ts` had `MAX_TOTAL_BYTES = 512 * 1024 * 1024` and `services/api/src/http/index.ts` had a second, independent `256 * 1024 * 1024` upload bound. That pair is the round-trip defect: incompressible content makes an archive ≈ its payload, so a 300 MiB export produced a package its own importer refused. Now:

- `RESEARCH_PACKAGE_MAX_BYTES` is the single value, exported and consumed by the export refusal, the import inflation bound, and the upload bound.
- `SCIENCE_AGENT_RESEARCH_PACKAGE_MAX_BYTES` overrides it, clamped between 64 MiB and 16 GiB, following the `SCIENCE_AGENT_API_MAX_OLD_SPACE_MB` precedent: a malformed or out-of-range value falls back to the default rather than either being ignored or letting one typo turn a clean refusal into an out-of-memory crash. **The default is still 512 MiB in this PR** — it moves to 5 GiB in stage 2, which is the only point at which the streaming pipeline makes it safe.
- The upload bound is derived from the cap (+5% and 1 MiB of slack for an incompressible gzip frame), and the inspection cache bound is derived from both views of one package (compressed + unpacked), so a valid inspect no longer hands the dialog a checksum the import cannot reuse — which used to make the client upload the whole archive twice.

**Refuse before packaging.** `prepareResearchPackage` charged the tar-block arithmetic, but the dialog could only see `estimateResearchPackageBytes`, which pads the manifest as `1024 + 256 * objects` and differs from the real archive in both directions (one 32 MiB object: 32.005 vs 32.011 MiB; 500 small objects: 901,632 vs 870,400 B). A dialog gating on that number can let a near-cap selection through and still get the late refusal. Added `researchPackageArchiveBytes`, which computes the exact tar size without hashing or compressing — hashes and object paths have a fixed width, so a manifest built from placeholders is byte-for-byte the same length as the real one, and the unit test asserts equality against `gunzipSync(export).byteLength` rather than against a second estimate.

**Server-side enforcement, not just the dialog.** A synchronous export is refused with `413 RESEARCH_PACKAGE_TOO_LARGE` right after the input is built and before any tar exists. The background task keeps its own late refusal (its revision can change mid-flight). The upload path answers the same stable code; the raw byte count is gone from the message.

**Both dialogs.** The preview response gains `maxBytes` and `archiveBytes` (additive; a client that ignores them keeps the old behaviour). Both export dialogs now:

- render the limit next to the estimate;
- over the limit, show the size against the limit, suggest the necessary export, and state the risk in plain words (long read, memory pressure);
- when `necessary` is already the selected profile, say that no smaller scope exists instead of offering one;
- keep both export actions disabled until `Export anyway` is pressed — the second confirmation the issue asks for;
- show localized copy for `RESEARCH_PACKAGE_TOO_LARGE` instead of the server's English prose.

The acknowledgement is keyed by revision + size, so any new selection asks again. Every new string exists in zh-CN and en, in both dictionaries (`apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/text/en.ts` + `zh.ts`).

## What this does not do

- **The 5 GiB default, and the peak-RSS evidence for it.** The exporter still reads every object into memory, builds one tar buffer and gzips it; the importer still inflates the whole archive. Peak RSS is ≈3× payload, so 5 GiB is ≈15 GiB — raising the constant today would convert a clean refusal into an OOM, which the issue itself predicts. That is stage 2: stream tar → gzip → file, stream gunzip → temp file with per-object verification, preflight memory and disk, then raise the default.
- **A round-trip test whose compressed size exceeds 256 MiB.** It needs stage 2's temp-file import to be meaningful, and this machine cannot allocate it (15.7 GB total, 4.8 GB free). It belongs to stage 2's PR with the RSS harness.
- **The per-file tar field caveat** (`MAX_FILE_BYTES = 32 GiB` against a 12-byte octal size field, ~8 GiB usable): unreachable while the total cap is ≤5 GiB, so it is left for whoever raises the per-object bound.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` clean for `packages/research-package`, `services/api`, `apps/web`, `apps/desktop`, and the root `tsconfig.tests.json`.
- `packages/research-package` unit tests: **13/13** locally, including the new ones —
  - the archive-size helper equals the real uncompressed tar, and the cap refuses at `predicted - 1` while accepting `predicted` (the ±1 byte boundary from the test plan);
  - the environment override clamps: empty/malformed → default, `1` → min, 999 GiB → max.
- The API suite (`research-package-http.test.ts`) now also asserts `maxBytes`, `archiveBytes` and `archiveBytes <= maxBytes` for every level/trajectory/memory combination. It is tagged for the shared plan, so its runtime result comes from CI, not from this machine.
- The dialogs were type-checked, not yet seen rendered: `UI` review and the rendered proof belong with the user's confirmation, and I have not claimed otherwise.

## Not covered by this PR, for the reviewers' decision

- `#1024` also owns a dialog limit line and proposes `archiveLimitBytes` as the field name. This PR uses `maxBytes` as #1152 defines it; if #1024 should own that surface, the field is additive and can be renamed before anything depends on it.

## Rendered evidence for the limit surface

Captures of the export dialog in the three states this change adds. They are
renderer-level: the dialog's markup with the repository's own `tokens.css` / `base.css` /
`primitives.css` / `dialogs.css` and the real `messages.ts` strings, rendered in Chromium.
They are not Electron-window captures and not a live interaction — the size and the
over-limit condition are the values the component receives.

| state | en | zh |
| --- | --- | --- |
| under the cap (limit line only) | ![https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1152/docs/screenshots/1152/1152-en-under.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1152/docs/screenshots/1152/1152-en-under.png) | ![https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1152/docs/screenshots/1152/1152-zh-under.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1152/docs/screenshots/1152/1152-zh-under.png) |
| over the cap (warning + `Export anyway`) | ![https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1152/docs/screenshots/1152/1152-en-over.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1152/docs/screenshots/1152/1152-en-over.png) | ![https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1152/docs/screenshots/1152/1152-zh-over.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1152/docs/screenshots/1152/1152-zh-over.png) |
| after confirming (actions enabled) | ![https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1152/docs/screenshots/1152/1152-en-confirmed.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1152/docs/screenshots/1152/1152-en-confirmed.png) | ![https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1152/docs/screenshots/1152/1152-zh-confirmed.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-1152/docs/screenshots/1152/1152-zh-confirmed.png) |

What the three states show: the limit line renders `512 MiB` rather than a raw byte count;
the over-cap state names the selection's size against the limit, offers the necessary
export, states the memory/latency risk in plain words, and keeps both export actions
disabled until `Export anyway` is pressed; the confirmed state shows the acknowledgement
and enables the actions.

Checked without looking at the images, since I cannot view them: the pages carry the
exact `messages.ts` strings with **0** latin-1 mojibake runs (the failure that broke an
earlier screenshot set), and the Chinese renders use a named CJK fallback rather than the
browser's implicit one.

**One limit, stated plainly:** this is a programmatic check of the strings and styles, not

Fixes #1168 (F1 half only).

## Problem

`confirmSettings` in `services/api/src/configuration/request-service.ts` read the clock twice inside one transaction: `confirmedAt: this.now()` and `record.view.updatedAt = this.now()`. The two reads could land on different milliseconds, breaking the `confirmedAt == updatedAt` invariant asserted by the `Manual settings` tests (`request-service.test.ts:427`). CI failed once in 7686 cases with `confirmedAt '...16.323Z'` vs `updatedAt '...16.324Z'`.

## Fix

Read the clock once (`const confirmedAt = this.now();`) and reuse the value for both `settingsConfirmation.confirmedAt` and `record.view.updatedAt`, mirroring the single-read pattern `propose()` already uses for `createdAt`/`updatedAt`. The existing assertion is kept as-is; no test-only relaxation.

## Proof

Base SHA (upstream main): `fc9e0b71` (reproduced and fixed on this head; branch rebased onto it after it landed).

Repro before fix — new regression test with a controllable `now` (+1 ms per call) fails with the same shape as CI:
```
AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: Expected values to be strictly equal:
+ '2026-11-16T05:49:16.005Z'
- '2026-11-16T05:49:16.006Z'
```

After fix:
- `node --import tsx --test "src/configuration/request-service.test.ts"`: **32/32 pass** (31 existing + 1 new regression test)
- `--test-name-pattern="Manual settings"`: **5/5 pass**
- `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`: clean
- Neighbouring `confirmSettings` users: `continuation-copy.integration.test.ts` 9/9 pass, `jiuwen-live-wait.test.ts` 12/12 pass (neither asserts these timestamps; run as regression scope)

Control: the existing `Manual settings true/false` tests on the real clock pass unchanged, and the replay path in the same test still returns the stored result — valid behaviour is preserved.

## Scope — F1 only

This PR fixes only the `confirmSettings` clock failure (F1). The other failure in #1168, the start-stack race, is #1135 and is already fixed by merged PR #1143 — untouched here. No workflow/CI changes.

## Risks checked

- `confirmedAt` is written only in `confirmSettings`; its only other use is a projection read-back, which reuses the stored value. The outbox `resume` payload reuses the same `settingsConfirmation` object, so it stays consistent.
- Same-class check: the only other `confirmedAt` writer (`src/evolution/proposal.ts:530`) already uses a single `now` variable.

Imported Evolve searches disappear when their run ID already exists in the destination, including when a read-only import is copied into a writable research session. ## What changed

- `restoreEvolveRuns` returns the source→restored run mapping; a colliding run is recreated under a fresh id with its event log, goal, status, budget and best node.
- Candidate sources are written under the restored id, so a run in the destination can still serve its source code.
- A run's result artifact now carries the restored id: the `evolve/<run>/` prefix of its name/logicalName/sourcePath and `originMeta.evolveRunId` are rewritten through the mapping, so `get_evolve_run` names an artifact this session actually has. The copy-integrity check compares the expected side through the same mapping.
- `buildConversationBranch` trims the evolve payload with the branch cutoff: only runs that finished at or before the selected reply travel, and only their candidate sources — a branch no longer lists a search from a turn it excludes.


## Validation

- **`tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` clean**, which is the `check:typecheck` slice of `UT` that this branch failed on.
- **`services/api/src/research-package-http.test.ts`: 21/21** (the import, repeated-import, continuation-copy, candidate-source, event-replay and artifact assertions), and **`conversation-branches.test.ts`: 6/6** including the new cutoff case, both run on this host with the `os:linux` tag relaxed for the duration and restored before pushing.
- **`evolution/package.test.ts` 16/16 and `research-snapshot-integrity.test.ts` 4/4** on the same basis; `services/api` and the root tests typecheck are clean.
- CI runs `UT`, `ST`, `L1`, `Coverage` and `merge-gate` on this head; the ST and mocked E2E results are the CI's, not claimed here.

## E2E user journey

The desktop journey (import → continue → open the Evolve card and task panel) was **not executed on this host**: it needs the real shell plus a full stack, which is not available here. What covers the same data path instead:

- the API regression test above drives import → writable continuation → restored runs, their event log, candidate source and result artifact;

The UI itself is unchanged in this PR, so no new screenshot is offered; if the journey is required as a merge condition, say so and I will say plainly that it cannot be produced on this machine rather than claim it.

1177.author: yuanzhou75
1177.body:
Refs #1152 — stage 2, in progress. This branch is **stacked on #1173** (stage 1); the diff shows both until #1173 merges, and only the streaming work after that. I am opening it now so the pipeline can be reviewed while it is being finished rather than as one large surprise.

## What is in this branch so far

The background export no longer materialises the archive:

- `ResearchPackageExports.createPackage(options, destination)` — the task opens its own output file and hands the stream down;
- `writeResearchPackage(input, destination, cap)` — tar → gzip → sink, with the package checksum computed over the compressed bytes as they pass, so the receipt is byte-for-byte what the in-memory exporter produced (a unit case asserts the two archives are identical and that a source is read twice: once hashed for the manifest, once written).

Peak memory on this path drops from *payload + tar + archive* to *payload + one chunk*: the two whole-archive buffers are gone. Cancellation and the mid-export revision check now delete the partial file instead of discarding a buffer.

## What is still to land before this PR can close the issue

- **Object residency.** The packager still hashes `PackageObject.bytes`, so the payload itself is still resident. Removing it means handing the pipeline object *sources* (CAS paths) rather than buffers — the piece that makes a 5 GiB cap physically possible.
- **Streaming import.** `readArchive` still `gunzipSync`s the whole archive and keeps views into it; the plan is gunzip → temp file → per-object checksum → CAS, so the importer never holds a package either.
- **Memory/disk preflight** before a large export starts, refusing with a clear message instead of failing half way.
- **The default cap moving to 5 GiB**, with the peak-RSS measurements the issue asks for (256 / 300 / 500 MiB, and the 5 GiB-class run) recorded here.
- The import side's bound must follow the same decision, or the round-trip defect returns.

## Why it is not `Closes` yet

The issue's acceptance criteria run through the streaming pipeline and the 5 GiB evidence; only the export half of that exists here. `Refs` is the honest state, and it flips to `Closes #1152` in this same PR once the items above are in — not before.

## Verification so far

- `tsc --noEmit` clean for `services/api` on this head.
- The streaming writer's unit cases (on the stacked #1173 branch): identical bytes to the in-memory exporter, a source opened exactly twice, an over-cap package refused before the sink receives anything.

1191.author: yuanzhou75
1191.body:
Closes #1190

A conversation branch keeps the candidate entries of the searches it carries, but not their source objects. The branch package then imports with `evolve:<run>:<hash>:missing candidate source object`: the candidate tree stays empty, `/api/evolve/runs/<id>/candidates/<hash>` has nothing to serve, and `get_evolve_run` loses `bestSource` — the same class of loss #1176 removed for plain imports.

## Why it happens

`buildConversationBranch` rebuilds the `needed` object set from workspace `objectPath`s, artifact-version `objectPath`s, `casHashes(records)` and `versionObjects`. `casHashes` collects a nested `hash` only when a sibling `size` is a number, and a candidate entry is `{ hash, objectPath, runId }` with no `size`. The top-level export lists those objects explicitly; the branch did not, and `prepareResearchPackage` does not cross-check records against objects, so the export succeeded and the loss surfaced only at import.

## What changed

- `services/api/src/conversation-branches.ts`: the kept candidates' `objectPath`s join the retained object set, so a kept entry always travels with its source, while a search the branch drops still brings neither its entries nor its objects.
- `services/api/src/conversation-branches.test.ts`: the fixture now carries real candidate objects, and the branch case asserts that the kept search's object survives and the dropped search's object does not.

## Validation

- `services/api/src/conversation-branches.test.ts` passes 6/6 with this change, run on this machine with the `os:linux` tag released and restored before pushing — the tags in this commit are unchanged.
- Mutation: removing the line that adds the candidate objects makes the new case fail with `the kept search keeps its candidate source object` (expected `true`, actual `false`); the line was restored afterwards.
- `tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` are both clean.
- The `os:linux` variant and the rest of UT / merge-gate run on CI.

1194.author: yuanzhou75
1194.body:
Closes #1182

Closes #1187

## Why

`pnpm --dir application test` is the gate in front of `pnpm --dir application dist`, the command that produces the NSIS installer. Four of its assertions asked for POSIX capabilities a stock Windows host does not have, so the gate was red for environment reasons — and because the CI step ran `test` and `typecheck` in one pwsh block, a failing suite was recorded as a green step. The same Windows job then failed one step later on electron-builder's implicit GitHub publish.

Both issues describe the same job from different ends: #1182 the four host-dependent assertions, #1187 the publish attempt and the masked step. This PR fixes all three paths together, because fixing any one alone leaves the gate lying about the other two.

## What changes

**The four assertions now gate on the capability they need, not on a platform guess** (`application/test`):

- `bootstrap.test.ts` — `dirWritable` and the `bootstrapPackaged` W16 case. After the `chmod(0o555)` fixture the test judges the fixture with a **write probe of its own** (`hostMadeReadOnly`), not by asking `dirWritable`; the skip happens only when that write succeeds (NTFS: `chmod` only toggles the read-only attribute), and the DMG degradation path keeps its coverage on hosts where the fixture is meaningful. Judging the fixture with the function under test would have made the assertion circular — a `dirWritable` that over-reported writability would have skipped the test instead of failing it — so the probe writes and the assertions below it stay falsifiable.
- `uninstall-data.test.ts` — the `bash -n` check is skipped when `/bin/bash` is absent, stating that the macOS 3.2 syntax check runs where that shell exists. It is the capability the assertion needs.
- `venv-launchers.test.ts` — only the `replaceVenvSymlinks` case is gated, on `process.platform === "win32"`: that block models a *darwin* venv (`replaceVenvSymlinks` is reached only from the darwin assembly and bootstrap paths). Without Developer Mode the fixture raises `EPERM`; on the elevated CI runner the link is created but `readlink` answers in the Windows dialect, so the relative-target comparison fails for a reason that is not the code. Here the platform gate **is** the capability gate — a POSIX filesystem that stores symlink targets as POSIX paths — rather than a guess: the fixture cannot describe a Windows venv at all. The trampoline, DLL and regular-file cases keep running on win32.

Four tests skip with a named reason; nothing is deleted, and no product code is touched.

**The CI step stops masking its suite, and the build stops publishing** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`):

```yaml
      - name: Test the desktop shell
        run: pnpm --dir application test

      - name: Typecheck the desktop shell
        run: pnpm --dir application typecheck

      - name: Build the Windows installer
        run: pnpm --dir application dist --publish never
```

The two commands are separate steps, so the suite's exit code is the step's result. `--publish never` keeps this gate build-only: `electron-builder` treats CI detection plus the configured `github` publish provider as "upload now", and this job has no token to upload with. Publishing stays manual, as `electron-builder.yml` already documents, and `.ci/ci-contract.test.mjs` asserts `/pnpm --dir application dist/`, which the new line still matches.

`.ci/ci-contract.test.mjs` also pins the split now — one step named `Test the desktop shell` running the suite, one `Typecheck the desktop shell`, and no `Test and typecheck the desktop shell` — so folding them back into one pwsh block fails the contract test instead of silently re-blinding the gate.

## Two premises in #1182 corrected

- **The cited CI job did not pass the suite.** In job `133716724096` (head `5058334f`) step 16 is recorded `success` while its TAP tail is `# tests 343 / # pass 339 / # fail 4` with the same four `not ok` lines, because pwsh keeps the last command's exit code. The four failures were red in CI too, unnoticed.
- **The cited job did not fail on this gate.** It failed at step 17 with `Error: GitHub Personal Access Token is not set …` from `GitHubPublisher`, after the NSIS build succeeded and the artifact was uploaded. #1187 carries that half of the story and this PR closes it with `--publish never`.

## Validation

Run on this Windows 11 host (Node v22.23.4), against the exact files this PR pushes:

- `pnpm --dir application test`: **343 tests, 339 pass, 0 fail, 4 skipped** (`# skipped 4`, exit 0). The skips are the four reported ids, each with its reason: `27`/`28` `host chmod cannot make a directory unwritable (NTFS)`, `248` `no /bin/bash on this host…`, `288` `models a darwin venv; POSIX symlink targets only exist on POSIX hosts`.
- Before the change the same command on this host was `339 pass / 4 fail`, matching the report.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` (the `typecheck` step): exit 0.
- `.ci/ci-contract.test.mjs`: the `Windows distribution gate builds the native Electron installer` assertion passes, including the new three pins on the split step (run locally with that file's `os:linux` tag released; the other failures in that file are unrelated absolute-path assertions that assume Linux and are not touched here).
- The read-only fixture is falsifiable again: with `hostMadeReadOnly` mutated to answer "read-only" without writing, `dirWritable answers true for a writable dir and false for a read-only one` fails with `expected: false, actual: true` instead of skipping (checked, then restored).
- pnpm argument forwarding checked with pnpm 11.1.2: `pnpm <script> --publish never` appends the two arguments to the end of the script command, so `electron-builder --win` receives them (a `run` + `--` form would insert an extra `--`, which is why the shorthand is used).

## Scope

Test-only plus the two CI lines. `pnpm --dir application build`, `assemble` and `electron-builder --win` are unchanged; the only behaviour change is that the nightly job no longer attempts an upload it never had a token for, and that a failing suite now fails its step.
1194.head: fix-1182-windows-desktop-host-gates
1194.title: fix(application): gate POSIX-only desktop assertions, stop masking the Windows gate, build without publishing

## Changes

Fix two failures in the Windows installer: a simple greeting can fail while loading `_greenlet` on machines without the VC++ x64 runtime, and the default scientific-environment layout can prevent managed Bash from becoming available before any command is dispatched.

- Use compact internal environment/revision directory names while retaining full public IDs, collision checks, existing prefixes and the pre-provisioning path-budget guard. The reported default layout drops from 283 to 235 characters against the 259-character budget.
- Pin the patched JiuwenSwarm dependency/lock to greenlet 3.5.5, which restores the static C++ runtime. Payload assembly exercises native greenlet execution and checks the version and DLL-name references, so the build machine's installed runtime cannot hide this dependency.
- Project `RUNNER_UNAVAILABLE` Shell results without repeated capability snapshots or escaped multiline diagnostics. Retain complete tool details, the recovery operation ID and independent Python/Shell readiness.

Existing Conda prefixes are never relocated. Previously created overdeep prefixes can still require rebuilding; new compact prefixes are used on all platforms. The greenlet fix requires a newly built payload rather than changing an already installed old payload.

## Verification

Candidate tree tested on Linux x86_64. These targeted checks were run before commit; the reviewed candidate tree is committed as head `3b051b4a84f27cbb1319450b652c281f037ffff6`.

- Runner environment paths/store: **42 passed, 0 failed** (fake provisioner; Windows paths simulated on Linux).
- Desktop launcher/dependency helpers: **11 passed, 0 failed** (synthetic native-extension fixtures).
- Blocked Shell projection and existing Shell diagnostics: **12 passed, 0 failed** (mocked tool callbacks).
- Runner/workspace typechecks, changed MJS syntax checks, final SDK patch application check, and complete diff whitespace check passed. The patched SDK lock also passed `uv lock --check` in an isolated replica without installing dependencies.
- Application package typecheck passed.
